title: Electronic Circuits and Sensors
summary: Electronic systems as input, process and output, voltage dividers with sensors, the transistor as a switch, and designing simple alarm and automatic-light circuits.

notes.text: An **electronic system** senses a change in the environment and responds automatically. It has three parts:

rows: Detects a change such as light, heat, moisture or movement
LDR, thermistor, moisture probe, push switch, microphone
Decides what to do with the signal

notes.text: A **voltage divider** is two resistors connected in series across a power supply. The supply voltage is **shared** between them in proportion to their resistances: the bigger resistance gets the bigger share. If one resistor is a sensor (an LDR or thermistor), the voltage at the point between them **changes** when the light or temperature changes. This changing voltage is used to switch a transistor on or off.

notes.text: An NPN transistor switches **on** when the voltage at its **base** rises above about **0,7 V**. Then a large current flows from collector to emitter through the output device. When the base voltage is low, the transistor is **off** and the output stops.

notes.title: A night light
notes.problem: A light-dependent resistor (LDR) and a fixed resistor form a voltage divider that controls a transistor and an LED. Explain why the LED comes on when it gets dark.
steps: In the dark, the LDR's resistance rises sharply.
A larger share of the voltage now appears across the LDR.
When that voltage at the transistor's base is high enough, about 0,7 V, the transistor switches on.
notes.answer: Darkness raises the LDR's voltage, which turns on the transistor and the LED.

rows: In the dark the LDR's resistance rises, the base voltage rises, the transistor switches on and the LED lights up
As temperature rises the thermistor's resistance falls; arranged in the voltage divider so the base voltage rises and the buzzer sounds
Water connects the probes, allowing current to the base, switching on a buzzer
Opening a door breaks or makes contact, triggering the buzzer

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: In a dark-activated circuit the fixed resistor is connected to the positive supply and the **LDR is between the base and 0 V**: in the dark the LDR's resistance rises, so it takes a larger share of the voltage, the **base** voltage rises and the transistor switches on. **Swapping** the LDR and the fixed resistor reverses the action, making a light-activated circuit. Always explain using the words **resistance**, **voltage** and **base**.

items: Use a **breadboard** for testing before soldering.
Check the polarity of LEDs, diodes and electrolytic capacitors.
Use low-voltage batteries (3 to 9 V) in school projects; never use mains electricity.
When **soldering**, work in a ventilated area, use a soldering-iron stand and wear safety glasses.

questions.memo:
✓ In the dark the resistance of the LDR increases (1)
✓ The voltage across it / at the base increases (1)
✓ When the base voltage passes about 0,7 V the transistor switches on (1)
✓ Current flows through the LED, which lights up (1)

questions.prompt: How does a moisture probe detect water in a flood alarm?
questions.memo:
✓ Water conducts electricity and connects the two bare probes (1)
✓ This allows current to reach the transistor base, switching on the buzzer (1)

questions.prompt: Give TWO safety precautions when soldering.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): ventilated area; use the stand; safety glasses; do not touch the tip; keep the cord away from the hot tip; wash hands after handling solder

✓ Two resistors connected in series across a supply (1)
✓ that share the supply voltage in proportion to their resistances (1)
